newsitem.title: USA: G7 sees no imbalance from dollar/yen level - George.
newsitem.headline: G7 sees no imbalance from dollar/yen level - George.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Sunday that G7 officials did not feel that the current dollar/yen exchange rate was creating imbalances.

Asked at a news briefing after the Group of Seven ministerial meeting here whether the present dollar/yen level was already a source of external imbalances, George said, "No, (there is) just a concern that it could."
George added that G7 officials felt that the exchange rate environment was in "pretty good shape," and that no need had been expressed for an action plan to deal with any future currency moves.
"That wasn't something we felt we needed to draw up -- an action plan," he said.
He said ministers had expressed the feeling at last February's Berlin G7 meeting that misalignments in exchange rates had been corrected.
"Things have moved on a bit stronger" since the Berlin meeting, George said.
"But I don't think anybody thought that what had happened since Berlin was a big move," he said.
He did say, however, that further exchange rate moves could lead to problems.
